solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

indicators.note: into says the word for see is placed inside the other pieces

parts.note: a van is a vehicle
lo is an old word meaning see or behold

explanation.surface: An instruction to peer inside a car parked nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: The starred clues belong to the Arthurian theme, so 'here' points to a place in the legend.
explanation.definitionFit: In Arthurian legend the isle of Avalon is the place where the wounded king was carried, so 'here' indicates that legendary location.

clue.text: First in song gets a curse

indicators.note: in says the letter for first goes inside the word for song

parts.note: an anthem is a song
A is the first letter, as in A1 for first-rate

explanation.surface: The opening line of a song carries a malediction.
explanation.definitionFit: An anathema is a formal church denunciation or curse, a synonym here.

clue.text: Drug needing trial — vain? (One hopes not)

indicators.note: needing is used loosely here to say the letters of the following words must be reworked into the drug's name

explanation.surface: A medicine needs a clinical trial, and everyone hopes the effort is not in vain.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of TRIAL and VAIN gives the answer; the parenthesis adds the hope that the trial is not wasted.
explanation.definitionFit: An antiviral is a medicine that acts against viruses, so it is a kind of drug.

definitions.meaning: fawning and smarmy in manner, unctuous
fish such as mackerel and herring are classed as rich in fat

explanation.surface: A grovelling person is likened to a type of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Smarmy people are called slick or greasy, and fish rich in fat are classed by that same word.

clue.text: East wind from North of Venice with city of Roman Britain

parts.note: the bora is a cold north-easterly wind of the Adriatic
cum is Latin for with

explanation.surface: A traveller notes an easterly wind blowing from north of Venice towards a Roman city.
explanation.walkthrough: The bora blows down the Adriatic coast, north and east of Venice.
explanation.definitionFit: Eboracum was the Roman name for the city of York in the province of Britannia.

clue.text: *He is a swallow, maybe, swallowed by a bee

indicators.note: swallowed by says the bird word goes inside the insect word

parts.note: taken as written: the letters of bee
a swallow dives, so it might be called a diver; a diver is also a bird

explanation.surface: A man is compared to a small bird that an insect has gulped down.
explanation.walkthrough: Starred clues are Arthurian: 'He' is one of the knights of the Round Table.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Bedivere is the knight who returned the sword to the lake, so he is the man the pronoun points to.

clue.text: *Where they negotiate for money — and time possibly included

indicators.note: included says the shuffled letters are placed within the currency word

parts.note: the rouble is Russian money

indicators.note: possibly says the letters may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Negotiators bargain over cash and over how long they have.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as conference talks, but in this Arthurian puzzle it is also the famous board at Camelot.
explanation.definitionFit: Talks between equal parties are held at a round table, and in the theme it is Arthur's famous board.

definitions.meaning: a punctuation mark, a kind of stop in writing
a part of the large intestine, an organ within the body

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a punctuation mark of two dots and part of the bowel, an internal organ.

parts.note: mod is short for modern, up-to-date
a red is a communist revolutionary

explanation.surface: Someone is described as having been a fashionable radical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' points to an Arthurian figure: Modred, Arthur's treacherous nephew who rebelled against him.
explanation.definitionFit: Modred is the knight who rose against his uncle, so he is the man the pronoun points to in the theme.

clue.text: Legend on the level in America

definitions.meaning: the American spelling of storey, a floor of a building

explanation.surface: A tale is said to be honest, as in an American's straight talk.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a tale and, in American spelling, one floor of a building.

clue.text: *In the matter of some Latin town

parts.note: as to means concerning or in the matter of
Lat is the short form of Latin

explanation.surface: A query about a town with a Latin name.
explanation.walkthrough: Astolat is the Arthurian town of Elaine, the lily maid.
explanation.definitionFit: Astolat is the town in Arthurian legend, the home of Elaine, so it is a settlement of the theme.

definitions.meaning: in Welsh the soft th sound is spelt dd, a letter written twice

explanation.definitionFit: Something copied is twofold, and Welsh writes its soft th sound as two Ds, a 'double D'.

definitions.meaning: an old past tense of heave, as in a ship that came into view
a seaside town on the Sussex coast, next to Brighton

explanation.surface: Someone relocated to the south coast of England.
explanation.walkthrough: Hove is a seaside town beside Brighton in Sussex, a county on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a past form of heave, meaning moved, and also the name of a Sussex resort.

definitions.meaning: God's guiding care, a topic of Christian teaching
RI is Rhode Island, whose capital city bears this name

explanation.surface: Names a topic taught in British school religious instruction classes.
explanation.walkthrough: RI is both the British school subject, religious instruction, and the US state Rhode Island.
explanation.definitionFit: Divine guidance is a theme of religious teaching, and the same word is the capital of Rhode Island.

clue.text: *He had family at the courtyard, old city

parts.note: kin means family
a garth is an enclosed courtyard or yard, especially of a cloister
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A man kept his relatives in a cloister yard in an ancient town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' is the theme's central figure, the king of Camelot.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary ruler of Camelot is the man the pronoun points to in this Arthurian puzzle.

parts.note: merl or merle is an old name for the blackbird
in means at home

explanation.surface: A blackbird in its nest faces a bird of prey.
explanation.walkthrough: The bird of prey shares its name with Arthur's wizard, the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: The merlin is a small falcon, a bird of prey, and also the wizard of the legend.

parts.note: a wave that smashes on the shore, read as one that does damage

explanation.surface: A destructive surge of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A large wave that crashes on the shore is named for smashing, so a wave that does damage fits.

indicators.note: make says the following letters are to be formed into something new

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A weapon used to make a young animal calm down.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of I with CUB RELAX gives Arthur's sword.
explanation.definitionFit: Excalibur is Arthur's legendary sword, a weapon of the theme.

parts.note: a Pekinese is a toy dog, so a hound that is not one might be a dog of low status, the one expected to lose

explanation.surface: A guess about what breed a dog is not.
explanation.walkthrough: A Peke is a Pekinese, a pampered lapdog; its opposite is a lowly, put-upon hound.
explanation.definitionFit: An outsider expected to lose is a lowly hound, unlike the pampered Pekinese toy dog.

indicators.note: against means next to, so the weapon word stands beside the fate word

parts.note: a lance is a long spear, a weapon
one's lot is one's fate

explanation.surface: A man armed against his destiny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' is the theme's most famous knight of the Round Table.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Lancelot is the chief knight of the legend, the man the pronoun points to.

clue.text: Graceful and neat, oddly concealing a limb

indicators.note: concealing says the shuffled letters hide the limb word inside them
oddly says the letters are arranged in a strange way

parts.note: a leg is a limb

explanation.surface: Someone graceful and tidy, yet hiding a limb in an odd way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' looks like a call for odd letters, but it is the anagram signal, giving EANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: an elegant person moves with poise and style, which is to be graceful.

clue.text: Girl from the Channel Islands (among others)

indicators.note: among says the islands abbreviation is placed within the word for others

parts.note: alia is Latin for other things, as in inter alia
CI is the abbreviation for the Channel Islands

explanation.surface: A young woman comes from Jersey or Guernsey, among others.
explanation.walkthrough: The Channel Islands lie between England and France; ALIA is Latin for others, as in 'inter alia'.
explanation.definitionFit: Alicia is a female first name, so it fits as a girl.

indicators.note: follower of says the darkness word comes after the monarch letter

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for king, a monarch
night is the dark time of day

explanation.surface: A sinister attendant of a king.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a man who serves the king.
explanation.definitionFit: A knight is the sworn retainer of a king, literally one who follows the monarch.

clue.text: Big and strong by keeping money back?

indicators.note: keeping says the reversed payment word is held inside the word by
back says the money word is read backwards

parts.note: a fee is money paid for a service

explanation.surface: Someone hefty and powerful hoards cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' gives EEF, the payment word read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a burly, muscular person is described as brawny, big and strong.

definitions.meaning: hire purchase, British buying on credit by instalments

explanation.surface: A query about buying on credit for a boy who never grows up.
explanation.walkthrough: HP is hire purchase, the British instalment-credit scheme, nicknamed this way.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for paying in instalments, and the name of the land where Peter Pan lives.

parts.note: vale is Latin for farewell
the Model T was Ford's famous car

explanation.surface: A servant says goodbye to a fashion model.
explanation.walkthrough: The Model T is the early Ford car, so 'model' gives T.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a personal manservant is an attendant who looks after his employer.

clue.text: Obstacle having no king for group of countries

indicators.note: having no says the royal letter is removed

parts.note: a block is an obstacle

explanation.surface: A barrier without a monarch is applied to an alliance of states.
explanation.definitionFit: A political alliance of nations, such as the old Eastern bloc, is a group of countries.

clue.text: *He removed the heart from wild beasts

indicators.note: removed the heart from says the central letter of the animals word is taken away

parts.note: boars are wild pigs, wild beasts

explanation.surface: A hunter cut the heart out of savage animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' is Sir Bors, one of the knights who found the Grail.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Bors is a Round Table knight of the legend, the man the pronoun points to.

parts.note: a gala is a festive celebration
had means possessed or owned

explanation.surface: A festive event took hold of a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'him' is Sir Galahad, the pure knight who achieved the Grail.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Galahad is a Round Table knight of the legend, the man the pronoun points to.

clue.text: Female insurgent retaining love for educationalist

indicators.note: retaining says the zero letter is held inside the insurgent word

parts.note: a rebel is an insurgent
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A woman revolutionary keeps hold of love for a teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: Friedrich Froebel founded the kindergarten movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Froebel was the German educator who founded the kindergarten, so he is a noted educationalist.

indicators.note: turned says the letters of the following words are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A teacher's lessons proved excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: the work of a tutor is instruction, the act of educating pupils.

clue.text: Rogue priest has what the corps should have

indicators.note: rogue as an adjective means wayward, so the letters stray into a new order

explanation.surface: A wayward clergyman has the team spirit a body of troops needs.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition rests on the French phrase esprit de corps, team spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase esprit de corps names the spirit of unity a corps should have.
